Social Climbers
Come join us on the 23rd September - 3rd October! Roger Hall, one of New Zealand’s most beloved playwrights, brings his trademark wit and warmth to Social Climbers.

A group of female teachers, joined by a reluctant daughter, set off for a weekend of bushwalking in the mountains. When torrential rain and a washed-out bridge trap them in a hut for three days, the stage is set for laughter, tension, and unexpected revelations.

Hall’s comedy gently peels back the facades we construct, exposing truths about friendship, aging, and everyday struggles. The play celebrates female bonds while offering audiences the chance to laugh at themselves through Hall’s self-deprecating humour. Infused with local flavour—Kiwi slang, cultural references, and familiar situations—Social Climbers is both genuine and appealing.

This insightful comedy is a love letter to female friendship and a reminder of why Roger Hall is truly a national treasure.

long_description:
Armenian Needlelace Workshop
Saturday 12th September, 4 - 6pm
11 Hopper Street

Join guest artist Lo for an exploration of Armenian craft and culture as we transform a simple needle and thread into beautiful lace! During the workshop, you'll learn the basic techniques of needlelace and spend some time playing with the form. You'll have time to complete 2-3 small (~5cm) pieces, either from a pre-set pattern or from your own imagination, while also learning more about Armenian history and symbols that can be looped and knotted into the lace. This workshop is open to all, regardless of cultural background or crafting experience. All materials will be provided.

Lo is an Armenian-American immigrant to Aotearoa and a lifelong crafter. From crochet to jewelry making to beading, their work is a multimedia meditation on whakapapa and the natural world. They are excited to share the joys of Armenian needlelace, an ancient craft that is as intricate and resilient as the Armenian women who have passed it down through the generations. This workshop is also part of a larger series of programming celebrating Armenian culture and bringing attention to the 100+ year history of the Armenian genocide and ongoing ethnic cleansing, hosted by Remember the Armenians.

A portion of all Generous tier tickets go towards free workshops for community organisations like the Wellington Women's House.

'It's in the Ballot' takes the format of the Kiwi TV classic 'It's in the Bag' game show and puts a political twist to it.

About this Event



Contestants of 'It's in the Bag' become political candidates in 'It's in the Ballot' Meet the Candidates.

Candidates choose a numbered box which has a question that has been submitted online by voters before the show.

It’s in the Ballot” is a community-led awareness and participation initiative. We aim to increase voter interest in the general and council elections nationally.

By using broadcasting and web-based technologies to deliver in-studio; online on Facebook, YouTube and Twitch; and edited as YouTube videos we aim to enable voters to make informed voting decisions.

This means you can send the weblink of the YouTube Video of your electorate show to your friends and whanau to encourage them to watch the show before they cast their votes.

long_description:
Dying Matters Week Whakaahuru - The Gentle Singers

We comfort people near the end of life with gentle, soothing songs. We sing by request, at people’s bedsides, at home or in care facilities from Wellington through to Porirua and Hutt Valley.




When we sing in communal spaces, we sing in groups of eight to ten. For closer “bedside singing” situations, we send a team of three to four singers.




Our request sings vary greatly depending on circumstances. It is our experience that every sing is unique, just like the person we’re singing for. Tones of Silence; Futuna Chapel in Black & White with John Walsh, Patrick Reynolds & Andrew Barrie
John Walsh and Patrick Reynolds

Architecture writer John Walsh and photographer Patrick Reynolds discuss their city walking guides and the heritage places they reveal, bringing together Walsh’s deep knowledge of Aotearoa New Zealand architecture and Reynolds’ distinctive photographic eye.

About the speakers:

John Walsh is a leading New Zealand architecture writer. He edited Architecture New Zealand magazine for a decade, and has written numerous books on New Zealand architecture, among them the newly revised Auckland Architecture: A Walking Guide, which features photographs by Patrick Reynolds.

Patrick Reynolds is probably best known for his exceptional architectural and interior photographs that appear in publications such as Urbis and Vogue Living. However, over the past 20 years he has developed a highly successful parallel career as a leading photographer within New Zealand contemporary visual arts. As an exhibiting artist his work is about New Zealand landscape, nature, architecture, patterns of seeing, and – just as importantly – about the art and place of photography.

Professor Andrew Barrie

New Zealand-born architectural critic and designer, Prof. Andrew Barrie discusses the research and publication of Block maps, drawing on his work as an architectural critic, designer, author, and educator with deep connections to architecture in Japan and Aotearoa New Zealand.

About the speaker:

Professor Andrew Barrie is a New Zealand-born architectural critic and designer formerly based in Tokyo. After completing doctoral studies in Japan, Andrew was a project architect in the office of Toyo Ito, one of the world’s most innovative and influential architects, and later at Cheshire Architects in Auckland. Andrew own design work is widely celebrated, having won numerous awards in both Japan and NZ—including a prestigious named award from the New Zealand Institute of Architects—and has been exhibited nationally and internationally. He is a regular contributor to architecture and design journals and has authored three books on the work of Japanese architects. He has made significant contributions to architectural culture in New Zealand, recognized by the award (with the Block Foundation) of the NZIA’s Auckland Cup for services to architecture, and his election to the Royal Society of New Zealand.

long_description:
Critical minerals, material solutions (Wellington)
The world wants minerals, but scientists around Aotearoa are working on what we could make instead.

About this Event



The MacDiarmid Institute is a network of leading researchers from around the country united in a common goal: to create and explore innovative, sustainable materials that will improve the lives of people in Aotearoa New Zealand and around the word. This talk will focus on critical minerals - raw materials that are essential to many existing and future technologies and have been making headlines in recent times due to increasing supply chain vulnerabilities. In this talk, hosted in association with the Wellington Branch of the Royal Society of New Zealand, we will present materials science solutions that are being developed and utilised right now, in Aotearoa New Zealand, to recycle, replace or reduce our need for critical minerals.

Speakers:
Professor Chris Bumby is Chief Scientist (Materials) at the Robinson Research Institute, Victoria University of Wellington, whose interdisciplinary research spans the fields of applied physics, materials science and chemical engineering - with a particular focus on Green metallurgy, hydrogen ironmaking, and superconducting machines. Originally from England, he completed his DPhil in Physics at the University of Oxford in 2005 before moving to New Zealand on a Royal Society (UK) Fellowship. Today, Chris leads the 'Clean Materials' Initiative within the Robinson Research Institute, is a founder and director of the start-up company Cullbeck Ltd, and a Principal Investigator at the MacDiarmid Institute.

Professor Nicola Gaston is Professor of Physics at the University of Auckland, and Director and Principal Investigator at the MacDiarmid Institute. Nicola’s research focuses on conducting quantum-mechanical simulations of the electronic and thermodynamic behaviour of nanoscale materials. She was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society Te Apārangi and awarded the Thomson Medal in 2023 for her contributions to low-temperature liquid metals research and leadership in New Zealand’s research, science and innovation sector. She also served as President of the New Zealand Association of Scientists in 2014–15.

Venue:
Lecture Theatre 2 (RHLT2), Rutherford House, Victoria University of Wellington, 23 Lambton Quay/33 Bunny Street, Pipitea, Wellington

long_description:
Te Wiki o Te Reo Māori Waiata Performance by acclaimed musicians 'Aro', Charles and Emily Looker
Award-winning Te Tiriti-based duo Aro create bilingual music that brings whānau together through waiata, storytelling, and connection. Made up of Charles Looker (Ngāpuhi, Te Rarawa, Ngāti Te Ata, Ngāti Mutunga) and Emily Looker, Aro blend Emily's honey-voiced jazz with Charles' full-throated, haka-inspired rhythms to create a sound that is both distinctive and deeply rooted in Aotearoa.

This interactive performance invites tamariki and their whānau to sing, move, and join in through original waiata, playful participation, and stories inspired by te reo Māori, te taiao, and everyday life. Whether you're hearing Aro for the first time or already know the songs, everyone is welcome to take part.

Aro remind us of our sacredness with expressions of their unique cultural identity. Blending Emily's honey-voiced jazz with Charles' full throated percussive sound with shades of haka, Aro's performance adds up to a warmth of experience, wholly original, anchored in Aotearoa that leave all who experience them with the feeling of having been let in on a special secret.

Aro are known for their rich harmonies, heartfelt storytelling, and bilingual waiata inspired by whānau, whenua, and te ao Māori. Since forming in 2017, they have toured extensively across Aotearoa, released five studio projects, numerous singles in between, and won Best Pop Album at the Waiata Māori Music Awards for He Rākau He Ngārara (2024). Their latest album Tāwauwau (2026) explores fantasy, faith, beauty, and longing, and has been celebrated as a finalist for the APRA Maioha award.

This event will be held in Ngā Paiaka Bleachers, Ground Floor, Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui. Free entry performance.

long_description:
Tones of Silence; Futuna Chapel in Black & White with Dr Malcolm Doidge
Dr Malcolm Doidge presents his 360-degree time-lapse photography project, captured in Futuna Chapel across the 2023–2024 equinoxes and solstices. A short film of the project will be screened, followed by insights into the digital processes behind its creation.

About the speaker:

After completing his studies at the University of Canterbury School of Fine Art in 1984, Malcolm Doidge worked for the New Zealand Correspondence School as an illustrator. He received his first commission from Lincoln College (now University), producing the work 'Ascent' in 1984.

In more recent years Doidge has taught Creative Technologies at Weltec (Wellington) and completed a Doctor of Philosophy, Inside Arcadia: An immersive virtual phantasmagoria. His degree was conferred by Massey University, Toi Rauwhārangi College of Creative Arts, in 2022.

His work has been recognised by several awards including the Wallace Art Award (2004, 2006, 2009, 2013 and 2016), the Visa Gold Art Award (1998) and he was the premier award winner in the NCC Art Award in 2002.

About this Event



The NZ ICS Cyber Technical Network will be running the 2026 NZ ICS/OT Cyber Summit on the 04 th November in Wellington, NZ (in person only)

Come along to engage with experts in ICS Cyber Security.

Topics will be relevant to:

Industrial Control System Engineers, Team Leaders and Managers
ICS/OT Cyber Security Engineers, Architects, Consultants etc.
Cyber Security Managers, Leaders, CISOs working in Industrial Organisations



DETAILS

Location: Lower Hutt Events Centre, 30c Laings Road, Hutt Central, Lower Hutt 5010, NZ

Date: Wednesday, 04th November 2026

Time: 08:30-17:00 followed by drinks & nibbles





The current summit agenda includes:

~08:30 – Doors open, reg, opening
~09:15 – Opening keynote
~10:00 – Three talks sequentially (plenary)
~13:00 – Three talks concurrently (streams)
~13:35 – Three panels concurrently (streams)
~14:20 – Eleven round tables concurrently
~15:35 – Afternoon Panel
~16:05 – Closing keynote
~17:00 – Drinks and nibbles

Current agenda includes contributions from:

Bhojraj Parmar (NZ) | Qubit Cyber
Paul Ganter (NZ) | Business Manager | SGS ECL
Pieter van Oudtshoorn (NZ) | ICS Cyber Security Consultant | SGS ECL
Contributions from NCSC



NZ ICS/OT Cyber Summit SANS Scholarship

At the NZ ICS/OT Cyber Summit, the SANS Institute will be awarding one complementary SANS course to a deserving member of the NZ ICS/OT security community.The scholarship will be awarded to a meritorious individual who has made a significant contribution to their NZ industrial organisation and/or the broader NZ ICS/OT security community. This form is to collect nominations.The submissions will be judged, and a recipient will be selected by a panel of judges. The scholarship will be given away in person at the NZ ICS/OT Cyber Summit in New Plymouth. The judges reserve the right to validate nominators and/or nominees. The judges' decision will be final, and no correspondence will be entered into. Submissions close Tuesday 27th October 2026 at 17:00 NZT. Late submissions will not be accepted.

To make a nomination, please complete the following form: NZ ICS/OT Cyber Summit SANS Scholarship (2026).
